subject: SIG follow-up: NorthStar - Business continuity & recovery details
messages:
From: security@northstarhealth.com
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-08T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: SIG follow-up - RTO/RPO and recovery evidence request

Hi Grace,

Thanks for completing the initial SIG matrix. The NorthStar security team has a few follow-ups specific to business continuity and DR before we can move to our vendor decision meeting next week: 

- Please confirm your target RTO and RPO for the Redwood hosted inference product when running in a single-region deployment and when cross-region failover is configured.
- Provide retention policy for backups and encryption at rest details for backups.
- Describe your regional failover approach (automated vs manual), typical failover time observed in drills, and whether live traffic cutover or DNS-based routing is used.
- Any recent test evidence (summaries) showing failover time and recovery verification steps (redacted OK).

If you can attach any short artifact (1-3 pages) summarizing the above, that would be ideal. We can accept a runbook excerpt or test summary PDF.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — our procurement deadline is EOD Friday.

Best,
Alex Jenkins
Security Operations
NorthStar Health

From: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
To: Alex Jenkins <alex.jenkins@northstarhealth.com>, security@northstarhealth.com
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-08T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up - RTO/RPO and recovery evidence request

Alex — thanks for the clear list. We're happy to provide concise answers and artifacts. Initial answers below; attaching a 2-page summary (redwood_sig_bcdr_summary_v1.pdf) and a runbook excerpt. I’m looping in Rishi (reliability) for test metrics and runbook confirmation.

High level: 
- Single-region targets: RTO = 15 minutes (application-level degraded mode; full service within 60 minutes), RPO = 60 seconds for KV cache-enabled state; 24 hours for long-term backups (snapshot retention policy).
- Cross-region (active warm-standby) targets: RTO = 5 minutes to begin serving from standby once failover initiated; RPO = under 60 seconds with asynchronous replication and continuous KV checkpointing.
- Backups: nightly full snapshots retained 30 days, incremental snapshots retained 90 days for compliance customers; all backups encrypted with customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM supported).
- Failover approach: automated region failover via our smart routing + orchestrator for most platform customers; for Dedicated/Private customers we support both automated (configurable) and manual runbook-driven failover. Traffic cutover is via routing and session-aware proxy; DNS TTLs are optimized to reduce propagation but we do not rely solely on DNS for critical cutovers.

Attachments: redwood_sig_bcdr_summary_v1.pdf (2 pages), runbook-excerpt-20270430.md (selected steps).

Next steps: Rishi will paste recent drill metrics for the April tabletop and the latest automated failover run.

Thanks —
Grace O'Connor
Head, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: Alex Jenkins <alex.jenkins@northstarhealth.com>, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-09T08:41:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up - RTO/RPO and recovery evidence request

Hi Alex — Rishi here (Reliability Engineering). Below are the drill metrics and clarifications you asked for. I’ve redacted customer IDs and included only aggregated timings.

1) Single-region degraded mode impact: 
- Degraded mode triggers if primary serving pool loses >40% capacity. In degraded mode we: reduce batch sizes, disable best-effort background prefetch, and fall back to smaller quantized model variants for latency-sensitive routes. This results in: increased per-request latency (~2–3x median on affected routes), possible queueing for non-urgent bulk inference, and temporary suspension of scheduled background re-embeddings. Feature-wise, text generation and chat remain available; large multi-turn sessions may see truncated context retention until KV caches rebuild. We do not provide automatic SLA credits for degradations that are within the published SLO window unless a contractual SLA is in place and the incident meets SLA breach criteria.

2) April tabletop + automated failover drill (aggregated across 6 runs): 
- Failover initiation (manual trigger or automated detection) → failover orchestration start: median 14s (p95 42s)
- Orchestration start → standby service ready to accept traffic: median 4m6s (p95 7m10s)
- Standby ready → traffic routed (session warm-up + proxy switch): median 35s (p95 1m2s)
- End-to-end median observed RTO (initiation → serving): 4m55s; p95 observed 8m54s.

3) Backups & retention: 
- Nightly full snapshots encrypted with CMK (customer-managed key) retained 30 days by default; incremental checkpoints every hour retained 7 days; extended retention windows available under Dedicated/Private contracts up to 365 days. Backups are written to encrypted object storage with immutability flags supported for customers who request it.

4) Replication & RPO: 
- We provide continuous KV checkpointing and asynchronous block-level replication across regional replicas. Typical observed RPO during drills: median 30s; worst-case observed (network disruption) < 120s. For strict RPO customers we offer synchronous replication options in Dedicated configurations.

Attached: runbook-excerpt-20270430.md contains exact orchestration commands and verification checklist used in the drill. I can extract the redacted log snippet if you need it explicitly.

Let me know if you'd like the drill CSV snippet; we can deliver it with timestamps redacted.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
